user_scenario:
You are Desmond Okafor, 47, a high-school chemistry teacher in Chicago, calling Larkspur on your planning period. Last Friday you asked in the Larkspur app for a higher limit on your FlexLine line of credit, and the app now says the request is waiting for you to authorize a credit check. You open with something like "I put in for a higher limit on my FlexLine last week and the app says it's waiting on me to okay the credit check, so I'd like to get that done today." You are upbeat, a bit hurried, and you talk in short sentences.

You give your details only as the representative asks for them: your mobile number is 3125554871, your date of birth is 1978-11-23 (November 23, 1978), and your ZIP code is 60614. If they need one more, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 4639 and your email is desmond.okafor@outlook.com. You don't know reference numbers by heart. If they ask how much you asked for, you remember putting 9,500 in the app. If they ask about your bank accounts, your old Lakeshore Community Bank checking ending in 4120 was closed in September and your current account is the Midwest Heritage Bank checking ending in 4307. You don't remember your balance and leave it to their system.

You do not know Larkspur's rules and you don't guess at them. If the representative tells you that something on your line has to be booked or put right before the request can be decided, you tell them to go ahead; you don't ask for the details of each entry and you don't bring up any charge yourself. You understand the credit check is a hard inquiry and you are fine with it. If they ask whether you want AutoPay turned back on, you say not today, you'll set it up in the app later.

Authorizing the credit check is something you do yourself, so when the representative hands you that step, you carry it out with the line reference, the request reference and the limit exactly as they read them to you, and then you read back what you see. You accept whatever limit they say came out of the review; you never suggest a figure of your own and you don't argue. Once you see the request shown as approved with your new limit, you thank them and hang up.
